 NIKE Sees Revenue Falling Through 2028, Targets $5 Billion Rebound by 2031

 Nike expects revenue to decline through fiscal 2028 , with a high-single-digit drop forecast for fiscal 2027 and a more moderate decline in fiscal 2028. Management sees fiscal 2029 as the start of a recovery, followed by growth above the market in fiscal 2030 and 2031. 
 By fiscal 2031, Nike is targeting about $5 billion in added annual revenue from a fiscal 2027 base, a 12%–14% operating margin and adjusted EPS of $3–$3.50. Performance sports are expected to contribute roughly $4 billion of the revenue increase. 
 The turnaround depends on clearing older inventory, improving full-price sales and expanding in growth areas such as running and outdoor, while addressing weakness in Greater China. Nike expects China to remain under pressure in fiscal 2028, stabilize in fiscal 2029 and be roughly flat by fiscal 2031.

 NIKE (NYSE:NKE) expects revenue to decline through fiscal 2028 before returning to market-level growth in fiscal 2029, as the company resets its sportswear business, reduces discounting and works to stabilize sales in Greater China. 
 At its investor day, the company outlined a plan to add approximately $5 billion in annual revenue by fiscal 2031, using fiscal 2027 as the base. It also targeted an operating margin of 12% to 14% and adjusted earnings per share of $3 to $3.50 by fiscal 2031.

 "We are not where we want to be," President and CEO Elliott Hill said, pointing to challenges in Nike Sportswear and Jordan, particularly in Greater China. The company also has more work to do on inventory, full-price selling and profitability, he said. 
 Near-Term Pressure Before Expected Recovery 
 Chief Financial Officer Dave Denton reaffirmed Nike's fiscal 2027 guidance for a high-single-digit revenue decline and adjusted earnings of $1.15 to $1.35 per share. Operating income is expected to fall faster than revenue.

 Revenue is expected to decline again in fiscal 2028, though at a more moderate rate, Denton said. Nike also expects operating margins to contract and adjusted earnings per share to decline modestly that year, partly because of higher product costs and limited ability to raise prices. 
 Story Continues Management expects fiscal 2029 to mark a turning point, with revenue growing in line with the market and operating income beginning to improve. Nike then expects revenue growth to exceed the market's pace in fiscal 2030 and 2031. 
 → Intuitive Machines' Business Is Taking Off—Will Its Stock Follow? 
 The company's plan calls for approximately $12 billion in capital returns through fiscal 2031, including about $2.4 billion in dividends in fiscal 2027. Denton said Nike's near-term priority is maintaining the dividend, while share repurchases could become more meaningful as earnings, cash flow and leverage improve. 
 Sportswear Reset and China Challenges 
 Nike expects performance sports to generate approximately $4 billion of its targeted $5 billion in incremental revenue, with the remaining $1 billion coming from Nike Sportswear, Jordan and Converse combined. The company is focusing on running, training, global football, basketball and outdoor, alongside sportswear. 
 Denton said four footwear franchises—Air Force 1, Air Jordan 1, Dunk and Chuck Taylor—generated approximately $13 billion in revenue at their fiscal 2024 peak. Nike expects that figure to fall to roughly $6 billion by the end of fiscal 2027, highlighting the risks of relying on a small number of products. 
 Nike plans to diversify its sportswear assortment and clear aged inventory, actions Hill said will weigh on near-term revenue. Jordan revenue is expected to be slightly lower in fiscal 2031 than in fiscal 2027, although the company anticipates modest growth for the brand beginning in fiscal 2029. 
 Greater China revenue fell 26% on a currency-neutral basis in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, according to Cathy Sparks, Nike's vice president and general manager for Greater China. She said local competitors have moved quickly while Nike's product and marketplace have not kept pace. 
 Nike expects further pressure in China in fiscal 2028, stabilization beginning in fiscal 2029 and revenue to be roughly flat from fiscal 2027 to fiscal 2031. The company is increasing local product creation and plans to focus its digital business on official flagship stores on Tmall, JD.com and Douyin beginning in January 2027. 
 Cost Savings and Growth Priorities 
 Nike expects its PACE productivity program to deliver approximately $2.5 billion in annualized run-rate savings by fiscal 2031, with benefits ramping up in fiscal 2029 and 2030. Denton put the program's implementation cost at approximately $1.3 billion, including about $300 million in severance costs already incurred in fiscal 2026. 
 The company expects to reinvest less than 20% of gross PACE savings. Its margin plan also depends on healthier full-price selling and operating leverage, partly offset by higher input costs. 
 Chief Operating Officer Venkatesh Alagirisamy said Nike aims to double the number of product units created in under 14 months by fiscal 2031 and reduce inventory by two weeks of supply. The company also plans to expand nearshore production and use artificial intelligence across its operations. 
 Among its growth initiatives, Nike expects more than $1 billion in incremental revenue from running and more than $1 billion from its ACG outdoor business from the beginning of fiscal 2028 through fiscal 2031. The company also aims to triple its India business over the next five years, Sparks said. 
 About NIKE (NYSE:NKE) 
 NIKE, Inc. designs, develops, markets and sells athletic footwear, apparel, equipment and accessories for sports and fitness, as well as lifestyle products. Its portfolio includes the Nike and Jordan brands, and it owns Converse, which sells casual footwear, apparel and accessories. The company sells products worldwide through wholesale partners and its own retail stores and digital platforms. Its offerings serve customers across a range of sports and activities, including running, basketball, soccer and training.
